focus: Geralt and Oreck fight off Federation Enforcers; Vel'thara designates Geralt as galaxy-wide threat "Ragnarok" before retreating.

The Federation enforcers moved with precision that spoke to training measured in decades, to coordination that transcended verbal communication, to capability that made them far more dangerous than simple military force.
Energy weapons blazed—not crude projectiles but focused particle beams that could punch through armor, disrupt shields, or simply vaporize targets depending on setting selected.
Override initiated, the Applicator announced, presence flooding through armor's systems with authority that came from understanding machines at fundamental level.
Geralt stumbled, barely catching himself before another energy bolt could capitalize on vulnerability.

He channeled telekinesis through the armor—the Applicator's presence amplifying power, Zaron's consciousness providing animation that made gestures more dramatic than necessary but undeniably effective.
Sand rose in waves, creating barriers and projectiles, obscuring sight lines and forcing Federation enforcers to divide attention between multiple threats.
Vel'thara stood at distance, observing, white eyes tracking every movement with assessment that went beyond simple tactical evaluation.

One of the Federation enforcers—humanoid but with skin that seemed composed of living shadow, features barely distinguishable from darkness itself—moved with speed that suggested teleportation rather than normal locomotion.
It appeared beside Geralt, weapon rising—
Not through conscious command.
Geralt spun through air like leaf caught in storm, completely disoriented, unable to determine which direction was up.

Geralt managed, using moment of distraction to channel telekinetic force against crystalline being—not trying to harm but to separate, to create space, to prevent overwhelming numerical advantage from deciding engagement through simple attrition.

The battle shifted—two against six was still disadvantageous but within realm of possibility, especially when one combatant was massive reptilian with centuries of experience and other was wearing armor that, despite adolescent unpredictability, still represented Aeon Keeper technology beyond Federation standard equipment.
the crystalline being called out, voice chiming through combat chaos.

But its tone carried less certainty than before—first crack in absolute authority, first suggestion that perhaps galactic law enforcement wasn't prepared for former slave who'd bonded with fragmented god and refused to hide behind mask.

It raised hand—signal that caused other Federation enforcers to disengage immediately, to fall back toward their ship with discipline that spoke to training that valued survival over pride.
The enforcer's tone carried something approaching warning that might have been professional courtesy between adversaries.
The ship's ramp sealed.
And within moments, the Federation vessel ascended—leaving behind churned sand and scattered glass sculptures and former slave who'd just been declared enemy of galactic order.

Geralt stood motionless, armor settling around him as Zaron's consciousness relaxed from combat readiness, as the Applicator compiled damage assessments and tactical analysis, as his own awareness tried to comprehend what he'd just accepted.
Within hours, every major system will have your identity flagged.
Within days, bounty notices will circulate through criminal networks.

Through every generation.
That showing my face, claiming responsibility, refusing to hide behind mask made them understand we're not just lucky slaves who got fortunate.
Would mean letting them define me through fear rather than defining myself through choice."

Oreck approached from where he'd been checking perimeter, ensuring no Federation surveillance remained active.
We're the beginning of something they can't stop through enforcement operations or threat classifications."
The compound erupted in sound—voices newly granted raised in affirmation, gesture-language forming cascades of agreement, recognition that they'd crossed threshold that couldn't be uncrossed.
